preamble: Replacement of a rhotic by the labio-velar glide [w]. It is attested as a historical change in mThachu, a Tibetic variety of the Melung subgroup (Sems-kyi-nyila group, south-eastern Tibetosphere), where the Old Tibetan initial r became /w/ while its rhotic quality moved onto the vowel (ri 'mountain' > wə˞). The adult southern British 'labial r' is labiodental [ʋ], not [w], and is not counted here.

examples.note: The initial r is replaced by /w/ and the rhotic feature surfaces on the vowel. Suzuki cites the Literary (Written) Tibetan spelling, which 'is considered to reflect the sound system during the creation of the Tibetan script'.
Suzuki gives only the syllable continuing rus; the rest of the mThachu word is omitted.
Suzuki gives only the syllable continuing rogs; the rest of the mThachu word is omitted.
